anna.li: Quick heads-up — during int4 onboarding for magnet-13b v2 I hit a reproducible misalignment when we resume long contexts (>8k). Steps and logs below, curious if anyone has seen something similar.

mike_r: can you paste the repro command?

anna.li: sure — minimal repro (on dedicated, quant-int4, no KV shard swap):
```bash
./redwood-bench --model magnet-13b:v2 --quant int4 --context 10000 \n  --resume-seed 42 --system "You are an assistant" --user-file tests/long_prompt.txt \n  --enable-kv-cache
```

sophie: what do you mean by misalignment? generation drift? token repeats?

anna.li: drift in attention offsets after a checkpoint resume. The model output diverges ~140 tokens in vs fp16 baseline. Logs show RoPE token index jumps (delta ~ +1024) when we auto-rescale on resume.

kai: hmm — is this only with prefix heavy inputs (system + long assistant turns) or any long prompt?

anna.li: observed on both, but more frequent if the prompt contains repeated long assistant blocks. I also toggled `--rope-rescale=linear` vs `none` — linear reduces severity but still off-by-some.

ci-bot: test-run 4990012345 started (ci: int4-onboard / magnet-13b:v2)

mike_r: any seed-repro? can you gist the small trimmed logs?

anna.li: pasted relevant snippets — note the attn indices and KV idx mapping around the resume point:
```
[RESUME] kv_index=8192 -> attach_start=7168
[ATTN] token_idx=8129 pos_scaled=8129 rot_phase=0x7f
[ATTN] token_idx=9153 pos_scaled=9153 rot_phase=0x2b  # unexpected jump
```

sophie: that +1024 smells like a window-tiling offset bug. Maybe our resume handshake subtracts wrong base when quantized (padding behaviour differs in int4 memcpy path).

kai: can you try forcing a full KV rebase on resume? i.e. recompute rotary base offset from 0 instead of applying delta? might be expensive but useful to confirm.

anna.li: tried `--rebase-kv-on-resume=true` — avoids the jump but performance regresses (obviously). Confirms bug is in the delta application.

mike_r: ok please open a quick reproducer PR with failing unit test (small context slice that demonstrates delta). Tag me and @kai. Add link to bench run output.

anna.li: will do. Also ran a quantization variance test: 5 seeds, int8 vs int4. Summary (generation BLEU w/ baseline):
- fp16 baseline: 1.00 (reference)
- int8: 0.998, no drift observed
- int4 (packed-symmetric): 0.942, drift in 3/5 seeds

sophie: int4 drop that big is worrying. Could be rounding + the resume offset compounding. Did you try alternate packers?

anna.li: tried `--quant-packer=zstd` and `--quant-packer=simple` — simple behaves slightly better but still shows the same offset case. Seems orthogonal.

kai: action items: 1) reproduce in a tiny unit test that forces resume + long prefix, 2) bisect the resume delta code (memcpy/stride), 3) compare rotary index calculations between fp16 and int4 memcpy paths. I'll own 2.

mike_r: for the unit test, include both `--rope-rescale=none` and `linear` so we can catch rescale interactions.

anna.li: opened PR 4892 with repro + failing test and a small harness: https://github.com/redwood-inference/redwood/pull/4892

ci-bot: PR 4892 — CI started (unit: kv_resume_tests)

sophie: thanks — I'll run local profile with nvprof to check memcpy alignment on int4 path.

anna.li: note for docs/bringup checklist: add a step "resume handshake smoke under quantized backends" and a small prompt to exercise it. Saved me an hour today :sweat_smile:

mike_r: good call. Once PR lands let's run a small dedicated canary across a few long prompt workloads (chat, code, summarization) to ensure no regression.

anna.li: sounds good — will follow up in the PR thread with more logs and a trimmed reproducer binary. Thanks all.
